pr_title: Add basic support for git and local dag bundles
pr_body:
This is a first pass at git and local dag bundles, and the bundle interface. These will certainly be expanded on (e.g. to support non-public repos).

Related: #42286
Closes: #42287 
Closes: #42288

issue_context.title: Create Local DAG bundle backend
issue_context.body:
### Body

We need a local DAG bundle backend, which will be used for backcompat with the DAG folder and for local dev. It will not support versioning.

### Committer

- [x] I acknowledge that I am a maintainer/committer of the Apache Airflow project.

review_comments: Airflow core does not currently depend on `git`. Tests don’t fail since it’s a dev dependency (IIRC).

I thought of this last night at dinner and then forgot. Thanks!

I also was considering whether we wanted this in core or a provider. But we don't have a natural home for it today. Something to consider longer term imo.
Done. Going to leave this unresolved for others to potentially chime in though.
Maybe we should have only the local bundle in the core while `git` bundle as provider.
Yeah, I imagine we will likely end up with a git provider before 3. Going to defer that for now though.

seems weird to have a `method` called `path` 
would expect it to be a property
also, not clear on diff between `path` and `dag_bundle_storage_path`

I'd actually meant to switch to a property, but never did that refactor.

I made `dag_bundle_storage_path` private and added a docstring. Hopefully it makes sense now?
why's this optional?
Explained more above, but 1) sometimes we always want the latest version, like when parsing DAGs, and 2) not all bundles will support versioning in the first place.
if hash is important it should probably be abstract too with docstring telling users how they should define it
TBD, it may not be. Going to leave it out of the ABC for now.
